observation_value_or_blocker: In primary mouse astrocyte experiments, IL-6 plus soluble IL-6 receptor induced reactive astrocytes and type-I-collagen culture generated collagen-I-grown scar-forming astrocytes that retained flattened morphology, N-cadherin expression, and scar-marker expression after removal from collagen or in-vitro beta1-integrin or N-cadherin antibody treatment. In transplantation experiments, collagen-I-grown scar-forming astrocytes induced surrounding host astrocytes to acquire the scar-forming/N-cadherin-positive phenotype; anti-beta1-integrin antibody reduced this recruitment. In a 70-kdyn T9 contusion model, anti-beta1-integrin delivered during the chronic interval reduced GFAP/N-cadherin-positive scar-forming astrocytes and increased GAP43-positive area.
observation_cell_or_model: Primary neonatal mouse astrocytes; CAG-EGFP collagen-I-grown scar-forming astrocytes transplanted into WT naive spinal cord; 70-kdyn T9 contusion SCI
observation_assay: Type-I-collagen-coated culture; GFAP/N-cadherin/GAP43 immunofluorescence; qPCR; astrocyte transplantation; laser-microdissection-associated expression
observation_perturbation: IL-6 plus soluble IL-6 receptor; type-I-collagen culture; anti-beta1-integrin and N-cadherin-neutralizing antibodies in vitro; anti-beta1-integrin after transplantation and from 14-28 days after SCI; isotype controls
claim_text_or_blocker: The authors conclude that scar-forming astrocytes persist and recruit neighboring astrocytes through a collagen-I-associated beta1-integrin/N-cadherin axis in chronic SCI, and that beta1-integrin blockade reduces glial-scar burden and increases the measured GAP43-positive axon-associated area. This is pathway and functional evidence, not purified collagen-I binding, alpha-chain resolution, a direct FAK/SRC assay, or a terminal TF result.
context_and_limitations: The artifact directly supports the registered receptor-proximal/pathway unit. It does not resolve a particular alpha subunit, establish purified collagen-I receptor affinity or occupancy, or prove axonal regeneration from GAP43 area. Evidence grade B; context L1.

observation_value_or_blocker: In adult female rats with C4 or T10 complete dorsal-column crush lesions, AAV co-expression of alpha9 integrin and kindlin-1 enabled sensory axons to cross tenascin-C-positive connective-tissue bridges, re-enter rostral CNS tissue, and extend toward the medulla; cFOS/VGLUT readouts and sensory behavioral assays supported pathway reconstruction and sensory recovery. The intervention was the joint alpha9-integrin plus kindlin-1 treatment, with no alpha9-only arm.

observation_value_or_blocker: After mid-thoracic T8 75-kDyn contusion in Col1a1-GFP mice, Col1alpha1-positive cells accumulated at the lesion from approximately 4-5 days, filled the GFAP-negative injury core by 7 days, persisted through 56 days, and formed the fibrotic-scar population adjacent to the astroglial scar. Light-sheet reconstructions and antigenic profiling placed these cells around larger vessels and distinguished them from NG2-positive pericytes; fibronectin distribution matched the Col1alpha1-positive scar population.

observation_value_or_blocker: SALM3/LRFN4-expressing cells coaggregated with LAR-RPTP-expressing cells; PTPdelta Ig1-3-Fc containing the mini-exon-B insert bound SALM3-expressing cells, whereas the B-minus form did not. In hippocampal-neuron co-culture, knockdown of all three LAR-RPTPs reduced SALM3-induced synapsin-I clustering by 85.2 +/- 3.0 percent, with PTPdelta showing the largest individual contribution. These measurements support SALM3 organization of PTPRD/LAR-RPTP-dependent presynaptic differentiation.

The registered PTPRD/LAR-RPTP organization claim is supported without inferring a defined PTPRD substrate, kinase relay, SCI transfer, or terminal TF.
context_and_limitations: The primary full text directly supports the exact SALM3/LRFN4-to-PTPRD/LAR-RPTP interaction and the associated presynaptic differentiation phenotype, while the registered contextual layer is retained.
